reason: contract_lock.py was changed so Orchestrator validates contract_surface_lock.surface_sha256 when present, while preserving fail-closed legacy git SHA and archive-tree behavior for older locks and non-fixture checkouts.
user_intent_alignment_summary: The user required Orchestrator to consume contract authority and execute workflows without owning canonical meaning. Surface-lock validation lets Orchestrator consume the Semantic Substrate contract surface without pinning every audit or decision-record commit.
diff_review_summary: The replacement preserves lock loading, manifest-first requirements, fallback denial, policy_bundle_id enforcement, fixture allowance, git SHA validation, and archive-tree validation. It adds contract_surface_lock fields to the ContractLock model and validates registry-defined surface hashes before falling back to legacy lock modes. It does not add canonical schema, lifecycle, promotion, routing, or AI front-door authority to Orchestrator.
why_merge_not_sufficient: The old lock model had no place to represent a contract surface id, surface hash, registry path, or validated contract-surface reference. A targeted replacement of the lock model and validation branch was required.
replacement_justification: The Orchestrator must fail closed on contract authority drift while ignoring non-authority Substrate changes. contract_surface_lock validation is the narrow mechanism that preserves that boundary and fixes recursive lock drift.
alternatives_considered: Continue validating whole Substrate commit SHA. Rejected because non-authority managed-patch/audit commits would keep forcing lock bumps.
Let Orchestrator compute its own surface policy. Rejected because Semantic Substrate owns the canonical contract-surface registry.
removed_content_summary: Whole-commit-only validation as the primary lock path
Archive-tree validation as the only non-git fallback
source_refs: Codex FAIL blocker: consumer lock provenance mismatch
